title: Tweeting with precision: A multiscale longitudinal digital ethnography of online cancer communities
content:
by Aymeric Luneau, Madeleine Akrich, Pascale Bourret, Alberto Cambrosio, Jean-Philippe Cointet

This study offers a digital-ethnography of cancer communities on Twitter, focusing on discussions surrounding precision oncology and biomarkers such as ROS1, ALK or HER2. Leveraging a comprehensive Twitter dataset spanning more than ten years (2011–2022) and comprising over 8M tweets from a variety of stakeholders, the research captures both the macro-level structural dynamics and micro-level interaction patterns within cancer-related online discourse. The combination of semantic analysis, user classification, and analysis of interaction patterns through retweet networks enables the identification of the roles social-media users play in disseminating information about targeted therapies. Our findings demonstrate emerging interactions between patient advocates and professionals, prior to formal recognition of innovative treatments. These dynamics are exemplified by in-depth examination of exchanges surrounding the foundation of a ROS1-positive patient group. The qualitative approach highlights how advocates and oncologists turn Twitter into a discussion space where patients find answers while care organization and clinical trial regulation policies are questioned. Precision oncology, online communities, Patient Advocacy Groups, social network analysis, text as data.
author: Aymeric Luneau
